clue.text: Drink I stirred to beat it

parts.note: a sling is a cocktail of spirit, sugar and water
the number one is written I in Roman numerals
shook means agitated or stirred up

explanation.surface: Someone mixes themselves a cocktail before running off.
explanation.walkthrough: SLING ONE'S HOOK is British slang for leaving in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang phrases for clearing off or leaving quickly.

clue.text: For one of the world's workers — charlady — dust is revolting

indicators.note: revolting means turning over or rising up, so these letters are overturned and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cleaner speaks for the world's toilers in complaining that dust is disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme says 'Saturday's child works hard for his living', so that child is one of the world's workers.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme assigns hard toil to a child born on that weekday, making it an example of a labourer.

clue.text: Use of satire like a club?

definitions.meaning: saying the opposite of what is meant, the mocking tone of satirists
resembling an iron, a type of golf club, with the adjectival ending -y

explanation.definitionFit: Ironical speech is a satirical tool, and iron-ish things are like a golf club made of metal.

clue.text: Permission to go ahead with new-answer to clue

parts.note: green means fresh or inexperienced, that is new
in crossword jargon a light is an entry in the grid

explanation.surface: A setter is allowed to proceed with a fresh solution to a clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A traffic signal showing go is a common idiom for authorisation.

clue.text: O Henry involved in recording

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: noting means writing down, recording
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: The writer O. Henry is caught on a recording.
explanation.walkthrough: O. Henry was an American short-story writer; here the letter O stands for zero.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter O looks like a zero, which is a cipher meaning nil.

clue.text: Withdraw from competition with no handicap

definitions.meaning: to pull an entrant out of a race or contest
a golfer playing off zero handicap is said to play off this mark

explanation.definitionFit: A horse can be pulled from a race at the last minute, and a zero-handicap golfer plays from the starting line.

clue.text: Round ox up, right?

parts.note: a round thing has the shape of the letter O

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: a yak is a Tibetan ox

explanation.surface: A drover asks if it is fine to gather up the cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking 'all right?' and 'okay?' both seek agreement.

clue.text: Noisy pool with disturbed water suitable for sea bird

indicators.note: noisy means the word is to be heard rather than spelt, so its sound is used

parts.note: a kitty is a pool of money in a game
a wake is the trail of churned water behind a ship

explanation.surface: A loud pool with churning water would suit a seabird.
explanation.definitionFit: The kittiwake is a small gull of the open ocean.

clue.text: Pupils out walking move quickly, and start to show false emotion

parts.note: a line of schoolchildren walking in pairs is called a crocodile in Britain
to tear is to rush along

indicators.note: start to picks the opening letter of the word show

explanation.surface: Schoolchildren on a walk hurry along and begin to display fake feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: Insincere weeping is proverbially attributed to the reptile that supposedly cries while eating prey.

clue.text: The little car we treat so badly

indicators.note: badly means the letters are arranged poorly, in a new order

explanation.surface: We mistreat our small vehicle terribly.
explanation.definitionFit: A small car with room for just a driver and one passenger.

clue.text: Bill, a rising player

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a tor is a rocky hill, a rising of ground

explanation.surface: A bill being brought in is weighed up by a rising player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' looks like a reversal signal but here 'a rising' is a noun: a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer on stage is said to play a role.

clue.text: Fabric that painter introduced

indicators.note: introduced means brought in first, so the painter comes before the other piece

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a painter
yon is an old word for that

explanation.surface: A painter brought in a certain cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificial silk made from cellulose is a textile.

clue.text: Patriot answers "I will always be there"

indicators.note: the letters sit permanently inside the words Patriot answers, read straight through

explanation.surface: A loyal citizen promises never to desert the country.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek letter that corresponds to our letter i.

clue.text: The record is held by Washington

indicators.note: held by means placed inside the grip of another piece

parts.note: DC is District of Columbia, the US capital Washington

explanation.surface: A notable record is in the hands of the American capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A vinyl record is a flat round platter.

clue.text: Position reserved, so to speak, in nursery

indicators.note: so to speak means spoken out, so the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a place is a position; cool means aloof, reserved

explanation.surface: A place has been booked for a child in a kindergarten.
explanation.definitionFit: A preschool group is a kind of nursery for small children.

clue.text: A consideration that's funny

parts.note: musing is thoughtful consideration

explanation.surface: A thought that turns out to be comic.
explanation.definitionFit: Comical and entertaining mean the same.

clue.text: Eccentric flag may be seen here

definitions.meaning: British slang for crazy or odd
a flag is hoisted to the top of a mast

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for mad, and literally the top of a flagstaff where a banner flies.

clue.text: Henry brought before court — it's for hoisting a flag

indicators.note: brought before means placed ahead of the next piece

parts.note: Hal is a pet form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal
a yard is a courtyard

explanation.surface: A man is hauled before a judge, and something to raise a banner is mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope on a ship used to raise sails or banners.

clue.text: Chalets built for storing books

indicators.note: built means constructed, so the letters are put together in a new form

explanation.surface: Holiday huts are put up to house a library.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolbag is a container for carrying textbooks.

clue.text: Hide the king outside

indicators.note: outside means the king's name goes round the other word

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king

explanation.surface: Conceal the monarch outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal skin, once tanned, is a material like suede.

clue.text: Doctor to call round about part of battery …

indicators.note: round means the shout goes around the other letter

parts.note: to yell is to call out
C is circa, about

explanation.surface: A doctor is asked to phone about a component of a battery.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry cell is a single unit of a battery with paste electrolyte.

clue.text: Girl had dress packed up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the result is read from the bottom, reversed
packed means stuffed inside, so the garment goes into the other word

parts.note: a robe is a dress

explanation.surface: A girl had her frock folded away.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, here standing for any girl.

clue.text: … said the man would attend

indicators.note: said means the word is spoken out loud and spelt as it sounds

parts.note: the contraction he'd stands for he would

explanation.surface: Someone reports that the fellow would be present.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to the previous clue; it plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed is to pay attention, as in attend to advice.

clue.text: Dress to boast about

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to brag is to boast

explanation.surface: Clothes to show off about.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is clothing, attire.

clue.text: Business has a way to succeed without effort

parts.note: Co is short for company, a business
St is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A company has a method for doing well with no exertion.
explanation.definitionFit: To freewheel to victory, cruising with little exertion.

clue.text: Unfortunately, I entered under another name

indicators.note: entered means went into, so the letter is put inside the other word

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately

explanation.surface: I regret that I checked in using a false identity.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb meaning otherwise known as, introducing a pseudonym.

clue.text: Initially hooligan elements abhor their pursuit by the police

indicators.note: initially means taking the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Thugs hate being chased by the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for police pressure on criminals, as in the heat is on.

clue.text: In Cornish town the Sabbath is relaxed

indicators.note: In means placed inside the town's name

parts.note: Looe is a fishing town in Cornwall, England
S is short for Sabbath

explanation.surface: Sundays are laid-back in a Cornish seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: Slack, not tight or strict.

clue.text: A monarch I discovered playing the mouth-organ

indicators.note: the letters are found playing about, that is rearranged

explanation.surface: A king is caught playing the harmonica.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonica is the formal name for this small wind instrument.

clue.text: Engage in conflict, lest there isn't another way

indicators.note: another way means the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Fight, in case there is no alternative.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter the lists was to ride into the jousting arena, so to join a contest.
